findings.title: Two sentences still say every summary carries a consent value, beside the new withdrawn-grant case that writes none
findings.recommendation: The walk's named limit now writes the emit with no `consent` field after a withdrawn grant, but two sentences still deny that case. `Consent recorded in consent-scoped lifecycle emits` (line 148-149) says "an abort at the consent prompt writes NO summary ..., so a summary that exists has exactly three consent stories"; and `Archive summary schema reference ships with the skill` in specs/orbit-archive-modifications/spec.md:167-168 says the field is "present on every post-capability archive emit" - the sentence that ships into the archive skill's schema reference, which the archive body's emit step is written against. Restate both: "a summary that exists has one of the three values, or, after a withdrawn grant, none (the named limit below)" and "present on every post-capability archive emit except one written after a withdrawn grant".

walk_entry.title: The withdrawn-grant recovery ("asks the user and records prompted") is undefined for archive and contradicts chunk constancy for apply

findings.title: The arrival table's needs-user and no-progress rows still overlap the another-command row
findings.recommendation: Row 5 now reads "`chain.next` names another command (whatever its `why`)", so an arrival at apply while `next` names an external review with `why: needs-user` matches row 5 and also row 6, whose "cannot hold here" is then false (it can hold, for another command). Qualify rows 6 and 7 as "not typed; `chain.next` is this command and `why: needs-user`" / "... and `why: no-progress`", as the walk did for rows 3 and 4; the claim "exactly one row" then holds.

findings.title: The consent marker comment in gates.ts keeps the old definition the walk corrected in the spec
findings.recommendation: The JSDoc on `consent` says entry into the gate's `before:` phase "requires an explicit user invocation" - the sentence the walk restated in `Gate declaration in schema YAML`. No task edits it. Add it to task 1.1's list of comments to update ("... or a grant by the project's `chain` setting").

findings.title: The walk's fingerprint stamps in .openspec.yaml sit outside every entry's edit record
findings.recommendation: The walk ran `orbit fingerprint` for the four carried requirements, editing orbit/changes/seam-chaining-grants/.openspec.yaml, but no walk entry names the file in its `file` or `ripple_cascade.applied`. A record gap, not a defect: the stamps are correct and validate passes. A later walk that carries a block can list .openspec.yaml in the carrying entry's `ripple_cascade.applied`.

commentary: Both regressions are the same pattern: a fix that adds a case left the requirement's own closure sentences in place. The withdrawn-grant limit adds a fourth outcome (no field) to a requirement that says three outcomes exist, and to a schema reference that says the field is always present. Qualifying three arrival rows left two siblings unqualified. Probed: every baseline hit for the retired consent wording lies inside a carried block (archive-modifications 137/273/695, run-summary-emit 633, lifecycle-consent 107/110, engine-gates 49, conventions 238/240); the program-PR scenario matches the baseline tail (commit, push, append; flip for per-change PRs only); validate --strict passes with both breaches declared; no @review: marker remains (the four hits are prose about markers). The residual diff since the external pass lists nine files, eight inside the walks' edit records.
